archive_16_001.speaker: narrator
archive_16_001.text: On day one hundred and seven, Yue took the written spring offer downstairs and asked to speak before the next supply report arrived. She had begun to fear that accepting after a delivery would look like courage, while accepting before it would look like faith. Neither description named what she needed to decide. The offered work had dates, pay, teaching hours and a return reserve. She wanted to know who would supervise her if Dai left for the warmer district, and how an injury limit would alter the assigned work rather than silently extend it.

archive_16_002.speaker: narrator
archive_16_002.text: Dai answered with the limited handover plan already under board review. The ordinary roster could be supervised by the appointed desk cover during her approved leave. Cultivation safety and clinical limits would remain with the qualified people named in the working plan, not pass to a chief desk merely because it possessed keys. An injury would be reported and assignments adjusted under the appointment's stopping provisions. The fifty-six-day term would still end on day one hundred and eighty-eight unless Yue separately agreed to something new. The answer needed the board's signature before it became a promise.

archive_16_003.speaker: narrator
archive_16_003.text: Yue also asked whether preparing the two-hour teaching session belonged within paid time. The board clerk had included delivery but omitted preparation from the draft description. Dai corrected that at once. A session which required inventing examples, checking permitted sources and arranging an assistant was not two hours of work merely because pupils occupied the room for two hours. The weekly preparation interval would fit inside the same roster, displacing other assignments rather than adding a private evening obligation. Yue marked the correction on her own copy, pleased by a question which had changed the work.

archive_16_004.speaker: narrator
archive_16_004.text: Tan read the practical assignment clause beside the draft. Light handling, inventory comparison and public teaching matched the work Yue had performed ordinarily. Reinforced work, if ever needed, would require the current external rig and task assessment, with its measured delivery limits. The appointment did not buy stage five as an unlimited lifting service. Tan said that sentence need not lead the public programme, but it belonged in the actual work plan. Yue had once enjoyed being asked what her realm allowed. She now preferred being asked which task and which ordinary part she could do.

archive_16_005.speaker: narrator
archive_16_005.text: Luo offered to help design the catalogue lesson under its admitted public sources. He would be contributing during his own assigned hours, and the assistant's presence did not become optional because he was skilled. Yue accepted one planning interval, then asked him what would happen when he disagreed with her example. He said he would tell her before the pupils arrived if he could, and during the class if accuracy required it. She liked that answer less than a promise to support her. It would probably be more useful on a difficult afternoon.

archive_16_006.speaker: narrator
archive_16_006.text: The chair approved the revised terms at the scheduled local meeting on day one hundred and eight. The spring account still reserved two hundred and eighty copper for the new fifty-six days. The extra thirty-two delivery copper came from contingency, leaving twenty-eight there; it had not eaten the wage reserve. Sixty remained assigned to spring qualified work. Meals would come through the accepted stock and supply plan, with its actual counts. The board could offer a practical funded appointment despite a difficult route. It could not promise that difficulty would never interrupt the work.

archive_16_007.speaker: narrator
archive_16_007.text: Yue asked for two days to take the final copy home to her residential room. Dai gave her until the agreed answer date, which was later than that. No one asked her to prove trust by signing while supplies were still below the mountain. She carried the pages upstairs, where her mother's letter lay beneath the pack strap she had repaired. One paper described work she might choose. The other described a house which would receive her. They did not have to become opponents merely because they named different places.

archive_16_008.speaker: narrator
archive_16_008.text: The carrier confirmed the day-one-hundred-and-nine dispatch only after the morning route check. The district's marked animal line remained sound within its conditional limits, and the carrier's inspector accepted the actual weather. The complete pack load, including its declared feed, handling gear and packaging, weighed one hundred and seventy-eight kilograms across five animals. Each individual load stayed below forty kilograms. The inspection covered the animals' condition and the route's combined live loads separately. The named food, charcoal and cooking wood finally left the warehouse, which still held the balance of the spring order.

archive_16_009.speaker: narrator
archive_16_009.text: The departure receipt travelled ahead by the checked message route. Tan marked first tranche dispatched and kept received blank. The train would use its arranged overnight stop rather than shorten the two-day journey by driving tired animals after dark. Its handlers carried their own meals and feed within the checked carriage plan. Dai sent the upper yard's present receiving report. The watcher confirmed the unloading supports and waiting line after clearing fresh grit from the turn. A real journey connected their two records now, and could still acquire a delay before reaching the second.

archive_16_010.speaker: narrator
archive_16_010.text: Yue walked to the winter village on her ordinary rest interval and bought dried plums with her own money. She had intended them as a gift to take home, then realised she did not yet know the departure date. The shopkeeper said plums could be eaten by a person who was undecided, which was among their advantages over promises. Yue bought a small amount and ate one outside the shop. Its sourness made her eyes water. For a moment, staying and going seemed less like identities and more like choices a woman could make while chewing.

archive_16_011.speaker: narrator
archive_16_011.text: He Xi found her by the market turn and asked whether the mule train had arrived. She gave the actual dispatched status. He said his school pupils would prefer an arrival story to a quotation. Yue said his route lesson might need an example of a parcel which had left but was still on the road. He sighed, then admitted it would be useful. His paid courier experience had already supplied several less charming examples. They walked towards the checked archive path, where the first real spring load remained beyond sight and neither had been hired to hurry it.

archive_16_012.speaker: narrator
archive_16_012.text: Tan's keeper returned on day one hundred and ten for the full drying checks. The agreed one-copper return visit came from winter qualified work, reducing it from one hundred and four to one hundred and three. Three of the six excluded sacks passed the soundness assessment and returned to the usable store. The other three stayed excluded. Tan recorded the actual bag numbers and tested weights before adding them. The keeper rejected Luo's joke that every sack should at least receive a certificate for perseverance. Wet charcoal had no opinion about the effort spent on it.

archive_16_013.speaker: narrator
archive_16_013.text: The drying room's extra two-sack heat issue was already closed in the earlier period. Restoring three sacks did not refund that consumed fuel, and the unsuccessful bags did not make the regained three disappear. The normal residence issues continued separately. The cook took one accepted sack from the original dry stack and left the recovered sacks in their tagged position until the attendant needed them. Their return made the present margin less narrow without changing the status of the approaching train. Tan could now say that one future action had happened and name precisely how much it had changed.

archive_16_014.speaker: narrator
archive_16_014.text: The train's intermediate receipt arrived later that afternoon. All five animals had reached the arranged lodging under their present loads. One food carrier's outer wrapper had rubbed against a fastening, and the handler had isolated it for the supplier's receiving inspection rather than mixing its contents with the sound shares. The inventory named the damage and retained the full issue quantity pending check. The handlers would continue only after the next weather report. Dai disliked receiving the small bad news before the large good arrival, then was grateful nobody had saved it as a surprise for the unloading yard.

archive_16_015.speaker: narrator
archive_16_015.text: Yue read the final offer that night without a lamp held over private files or a storm asking for her calf. The preparation interval was written, the supervision named and the wage reserve real. She thought of her mother's underlined recovering, Tan's old pattern and the pupil who had corrected her snail aloud. Another season would give her work she wanted to learn, and it would delay a home visit she also wanted. She could accept that cost honestly or decline it honestly. The contract did not supply the personal answer beneath its careful lines.

archive_16_016.speaker: narrator
archive_16_016.text: She put a small plum beside the home letter and laughed at the shopkeeper's advice. Then she wrote the first sentence of a reply: I am considering staying through the next spring term, which has an actual final day. She stopped before turning considering into a hidden decision. Tomorrow's arrival would tell the archive something important about its stores. It would not sign her appointment. She lowered the lamp, leaving the plums wrapped and the final offer on the table, where morning could find both objects without making either one a test of bravery.

archive_16_017.speaker: narrator
archive_16_017.text: The first mule appeared below the turn on day one hundred and eleven with snow clinging to its whiskers. It stopped exactly where the guide stopped, unimpressed by the archive's excitement. Behind it came four more animals, their covered loads making five dark humps against the white path. The lead handler lifted a mittened hand. The watcher checked the waiting line and called the unloading crew. Yue could hear buckles striking softly beneath cloth. After so many letters about movement, the noise of actual leather seemed startlingly loud.

archive_16_018.speaker: narrator
archive_16_018.text: He Xi stood too near the turn until the guide pointed to the marked waiting space. He moved, then attempted to look as though he had gone there to supervise the view. The first mule looked at him. Its handler said the animal was called Nettle and could recognise an inexperienced supervisor at a hundred paces. He Xi asked whether it recognised the experienced kind. The handler said it disliked them even more. Tan laughed from the store door, where she was waiting with the accepted inventory rather than a welcome speech.

archive_16_019.speaker: he_xi
archive_16_019.text: I have carried messages about you for nearly two weeks, Nettle. I think that should count as a useful introduction. You need not approve of my supervision, but I would appreciate your walking towards the place where Tan wants the sacks. She has a ruler, and it is more frightening than my mother's questions about lost delivery charges.

archive_16_020.speaker: narrator
archive_16_020.text: The handler led Nettle one cleared interval at a time. The other animals remained under the second handler and guide at the safe waiting points; none crowded the narrow yard turn. Workers loosened the first load on its supported side before lifting the covered pieces to the receiving boards. Yue reached for a strap and the handler caught her sleeve, gently but quickly. The fastening belonged to his load sequence. She drew back, thanked him and waited for the piece he actually handed her: a small dry label pouch.

archive_16_021.speaker: narrator
archive_16_021.text: Tan checked the charcoal sacks as they came off. The cloth was sound, the weights matched the five-kilogram specification and the fuel inside passed the accepted receiving condition. She entered eight. The cook took the food carriers with her assistant, looking first for the oil jars' guards and the distinct vegetable wrapping. She held an onion to her nose and smiled so fiercely that Luo stepped back. He said he had never seen anyone threaten an onion with affection. She told him it was a private matter between cooks and vegetables.

archive_16_022.speaker: tan_ke
archive_16_022.text: Eight sound sacks, and do not stack them against the new threshold merely because it now has a handsome strip. Put them in the marked dry bay. Luo, the tag pouch goes on the rack before anybody borrows its string. He Xi, Nettle has no need for an onion. Yue, help the cook compare the component groups. You are the only person here who has not yet proposed feeding some part of this delivery to a joke.

archive_16_023.speaker: narrator
archive_16_023.text: The rubbed food carrier had a broken inner wrapper as well as the damaged outer cover. Road grit had reached three complete share groups. The cook kept those groups apart and accepted the remaining one hundred and seventeen shares. She did not salvage a visibly spoiled component merely because most of its neighbours were sound. The handler watched the check, then signed the condition note naming the isolated carrier he had reported at the intermediate stop. He had hoped the inner wrap would hold. The cook said he had done right to keep it separate.

archive_16_024.speaker: narrator
archive_16_024.text: The supplier's accepted delivery terms covered replacement of the three rejected shares with the remaining consignment. Tan wrote four hundred and eighty-three food shares on the balance request, the original four hundred and eighty plus the three replacements. The first receipt recorded one hundred and seventeen accepted, not one hundred and twenty. The cook read both numbers back while the handler held the paper against a dry board. Neither had appetite for a dispute. She had beans to store; he had animals to water at the arranged lodging before the afternoon weather changed.

archive_16_025.speaker: narrator
archive_16_025.text: Ten dry cooking bundles passed their own check and went into the kitchen's separate bay. Their arrival pleased the cook more quietly than the onions. She ran her hand along a sound bundle, then told her assistant where the earlier stock should be used first. The new goods smelled of the lower warehouse's dry wood and fresh wrapping. Yue helped place the lighter component groups on their assigned shelves. The floor felt crowded without being chaotic, and for the first time she saw the pending spaces contain things which would answer hunger.

archive_16_026.speaker: narrator
archive_16_026.text: Luo tried to thank the guide by offering a hot archive meal. The guide showed him the carrier's lodging arrangement and said the meal was already waiting below with the animals' feed. There was no need to change plans now. Luo accepted the answer without turning his offer into an argument about generosity. He gave the handler the signed receiving receipt and the condition copy. The train left the yard under its own crew, lighter and still organised. Nettle glanced back once, perhaps at the onion, perhaps at nothing the humans deserved to interpret.

archive_16_027.speaker: luo_zhimo
archive_16_027.text: I shall put Nettle in no catalogue. She has expressed a clear opinion of public access, and I suspect she would eat any slip we made in order to prove that the collection remained hers. I will, however, remember the handler who noticed the torn wrapper before arriving. It made the receiving check shorter. Please tell her that, He Xi, if your next paid route reaches their lodging before they leave.

archive_16_028.speaker: narrator
archive_16_028.text: He Xi promised no extra detour. He would check his actual route. The answer made Luo grin, and the cook handed the boy his returned delivery cover rather than a bowl. He had his family's midday meal waiting in the village. He went down the checked path after the train, carefully beyond the handlers' work space. His long plait swung against his coat. Yue heard him ask Nettle whether she charged for carrying messages, and heard the handler answer that her rates were dreadful and included very little conversation.

archive_16_029.speaker: narrator
archive_16_029.text: Inside, the cook opened the first sound onion group for the ordinary resident pot. The shares issued that day still belonged in the daily count; receiving a large box did not turn its contents into a feast outside the ledger. She did change the seasoning. The recovering clerk ate slowly and said it tasted like a room with another window. Tan said onions rarely deserved such a review. He told her she could eat a dry catalogue heading next time. Their quarrel was comfortable enough for Dai to sit down without bringing the receipt to the table.

archive_16_030.speaker: narrator
archive_16_030.text: Yue swallowed the first mouthful and realised how much of the week's anxiety had settled in her jaw. The food was not richer than ordinary food at home. It tasted newly possible because somebody had checked a route, tied a load, stopped at the right lodging and brought it intact enough for the kitchen to use. She did not make that sequence a speech. She asked for the onion bowl when it reached her end of the table and let the cook see her enjoyment. The cook nodded as though she had received a satisfactory receipt.

archive_16_031.speaker: narrator
archive_16_031.text: After the pot was cleared, Dai and Tan closed the first-tranche receiving record. Eight charcoal sacks, one hundred and seventeen food shares and ten cooking bundles had actually arrived. Three rejected food shares would be replaced in the balance. The goods were divided by accepted components and assigned dry storage. The revised delivery price remained as agreed. Dai signed, then pushed her chair back with a sound of real fatigue. Waiting had occupied her in ways she had not noticed until an empty pending field finally became an ordinary date.

archive_16_032.speaker: narrator
archive_16_032.text: Sun came to the public session later that afternoon with a line she had cut from another story. She was not offering the cut line to the archive. She wanted to know whether the bookshop could supply an ordinary small notebook after the next carriage delivery. Luo checked the public trade directory and gave her the shop's actual contact. She explained that she had begun a story about a woman whose umbrella disliked sunshine. He asked whether the umbrella had a contract. She said it had a hole and wished he would stop confusing every inconvenience with a profession.

archive_16_033.speaker: sun_nian
archive_16_033.text: There are umbrellas which have spent their whole lives being called useless because the owner opens them in the wrong weather. This one has a hole, so it is also useless in the right weather. I have not decided what it wants. Perhaps a new owner, perhaps a patch, perhaps a day when nobody asks it to explain why it has not fulfilled the forecast. I shall write it in the notebook if the shop has one. You need not acquire the notebook before it contains a sentence.

archive_16_034.speaker: narrator
archive_16_034.text: Yue laughed, then asked whether the umbrella could become a bowl. Sun said that was the sort of question authors received when one story had gone well. They were expected to make every new thing resemble it. She wanted the umbrella to remain an umbrella until it became annoying enough to change itself. The cook, passing the doorway, said she had an umbrella annoying enough already. Sun asked its colour. The cook gave her no permission to make it autobiographical, which pleased both of them.

archive_16_035.speaker: narrator
archive_16_035.text: The room's delight in the arrival ebbed towards ordinary tiredness. Tan checked the repaired threshold again after the day's traffic. The brush had been used, and no new meltwater had reached the accepted sacks. The drying bay still held three excluded bags, each with its own tag. Yue swept the receiving boards and found a small onion peel lodged in a crack. She removed it before putting the board away. The work had no witnesses by then. It was nevertheless part of making tomorrow's ordinary meal possible.

archive_16_036.speaker: narrator
archive_16_036.text: In her room, the dried plums had shifted inside their wrapper. Yue took one out and held it above the spring offer like a ridiculous seal. She had once wanted decisions to arrive accompanied by certainty, perhaps through a trial which made every alternative obviously wrong. Here the mule train had arrived partly sound, the remaining order still depended on the road and home still lay in another direction. She knew enough to choose, which was a smaller thing than knowing how the whole season would end.

archive_16_037.speaker: lin_yue
archive_16_037.text: I want to teach the lesson we have been making, and I want to see the spring restoration through its actual handover. I also want to go home. If I stay, I shall have to say that I am choosing to delay the visit, not that the archive has prevented it. I think I can say that. I do not want the contract to become another story in which I keep promising myself a date after the last unfinished file.

archive_16_038.speaker: narrator
archive_16_038.text: She spoke the words quietly enough that the empty room could hear them without responding. Then she wrote a plain answer on her own copy: accepted with the revised preparation interval and supervision plan. She did not sign the institution's copy alone at midnight. Tomorrow she would go to the public office, compare the final terms and place the accepted page where both parties could retain it. Her home letter would name day one hundred and eighty-eight as the term's finish, and leave travel time subject to the actual safe route.

archive_16_039.speaker: narrator
archive_16_039.text: Beyond the window, the handlers' lodging light appeared low in the village. The animals would rest there before returning by their checked plan. Yue watched the light until it blurred, then shut the curtain. She had eaten, the ordinary calf was quiet and the work she wanted had become a decision she could explain. She slept without placing her pack beside the door as though leaving immediately were the only proof she remained free. The pack hung where she had repaired its strap, ready for a future journey which now had a stated boundary.

archive_16_040.speaker: narrator
archive_16_040.text: Yue signed the final extension on day one hundred and twelve. Dai compared the teaching preparation clause, the supervision plan and the fifty-six dates against Yue's retained copy before both signed. The spring wage reserve stayed two hundred and eighty copper, and the original return-fare reserve remained intact. Yue took her copy upstairs and finished the home letter with the decision made plain. She would work through day one hundred and eighty-eight, then arrange the safe return journey. Her mother could disagree with that choice without having to guess what it was.

archive_16_041.speaker: narrator
archive_16_041.text: The first small teaching rehearsal took place that afternoon within Yue's assigned winter planning hours. It was not yet the spring programme. The teacher brought six pupils for the agreed short trial, with permission for the borrowed room and its ordinary public materials. They would return to their school kitchen afterwards rather than become archive lunch guests. The smallest pupil demanded to know whether the archive contained a dragon. Luo said it contained several dragon headings. The pupil asked whether any of them had bitten somebody. Luo said mostly the people who tried to interpret them.

archive_16_042.speaker: narrator
archive_16_042.text: Yue had laid out three invented slips beside a dated admitted public map. The slips named an old bridge field, an east district road and a source with no district heading. She began explaining the difference before the pupils sat down. Tan caught her eye from the assistant's place. Yue stopped and invited them to look first. The child with the snail put a finger above the missing heading without touching the page. Another pupil asked why the old bridge was called old if the new bridge did not appear on that map.

archive_16_043.speaker: lin_yue
archive_16_043.text: That is a useful question. Which date belongs to the map, and which date belongs to the slip? Look at both before choosing what the word old means. You may find that the two pieces were made when people meant different bridges. I shall wait while you compare them. Luo has agreed to be the person we ask if the source cannot answer by itself, and he is allowed to tell us he needs another record.

archive_16_044.speaker: narrator
archive_16_044.text: The pupils found two dates and an ambiguous district name. One declared the slip a lie. Another said perhaps it had just been written by somebody who already knew which bridge they meant. The second answer was less exciting and closer to the actual problem. Yue resisted awarding the first child a dramatic correction. She asked what a future reader would need. The snail author said a name which did not expect the reader to live in the writer's head. Luo wrote that on the trial sheet and asked whether he could quote the phrase in the class summary.

archive_16_045.speaker: narrator
archive_16_045.text: The child gave permission for that sentence with her name. She did not offer her whole unfinished snail story. The smallest pupil, disappointed by the absent dragon, asked whether an archive could keep a person who had the answer. Dai was standing at the back door and almost replied. Tan said people could work in an archive and still go home. The pupil asked why they kept so many words if people remained necessary. Yue looked at Luo, who was trying unsuccessfully not to laugh. It was a better question than any she had prepared.

archive_16_046.speaker: luo_zhimo
archive_16_046.text: Because people forget, move away, disagree and sometimes die before we learn to ask them properly. Words help another person begin. They do not always finish the work. A map can show a bridge which has since fallen, and an answer from me can miss a record I have never seen. Today you have the opportunity to discover one of those misses before I have had time to arrange a more impressive explanation.

archive_16_047.speaker: narrator
archive_16_047.text: One pupil proposed cutting the date from an invented slip and giving it to a younger class as a puzzle. Yue asked whether the younger class would know it was invented. The pupil said they should be told, otherwise it would be a mean puzzle. He looked at the adults as though the rule were obvious. Tan kept the real source map beyond the cutting paper and offered ordinary scrap for the proposed exercise. They made a deliberately incomplete example together, with its invented status written at the top. The pupils argued over the title rather than the facts.

archive_16_048.speaker: narrator
archive_16_048.text: The smallest pupil reached for Tan's ruler and knocked an empty tag box off the low table. Labels scattered around the stool legs. He froze, expecting an adult to tell him he had endangered the archive. Tan set the ruler down and asked him to help collect the empty labels from the safe floor space. The original map had remained on its protected support. Yue moved the tag box farther from the elbow line before continuing. The class resumed with a less elegant table and a child willing to ask another question.

archive_16_049.speaker: tan_ke
archive_16_049.text: This ruler is very good at measuring paper and very poor at stopping an elbow. We should put it where you can see the marks without reaching across the box. Help me choose the position. Then I shall tell Yue that arranging a room is part of teaching, so she will stop regarding the table as a place where an explanation happens by magic.

archive_16_050.speaker: narrator
archive_16_050.text: At the end, the teacher asked each pupil to name a question which had helped. None named the line Yue had thought would be the lesson's centre. Two chose the map date, one chose the district heading and the smallest chose whether dragons could leave. The teacher included his answer because it described the question he had actually asked. Yue felt a brief foolish disappointment and then wrote the responses exactly. The rehearsal had become something people did in the room, less obedient than the lesson she had imagined alone beside her plums.

archive_16_051.speaker: narrator
archive_16_051.text: He Xi waited by the door with his own school price sheet. The teacher had agreed to let him try its opening after the archive rehearsal, before the pupils went home. He began with the neighbour who needed a free delivery and asked who paid for the courier's boots. The pupils nominated the neighbour, the courier and the mule. He had no answer prepared for the mule. He said its handler would probably object to paying for human boots. The smallest pupil asked whether Nettle could be invited to the next lesson.

archive_16_052.speaker: narrator
archive_16_052.text: The teacher declined the animal invitation for the room's size and ordinary safety, then promised the pupils a route drawing. He Xi pointed to the undelivered-parcel space his mother had made him add. A pupil asked whether a courier still received payment if the customer had written the wrong address. He Xi looked towards the door as though his mother might appear with the exact rule. She did not. He explained the distinction between the accepted travel task and a further route, then said he would verify the terms before teaching a fixed price. The teacher marked the unanswered question.

archive_16_053.speaker: narrator
archive_16_053.text: Yue felt grateful for his visible pause. Her own pause at the map had seemed a teacher's failure until the pupils used it to think. He Xi's made his lesson less polished and more believable. After the children left for the school pot, she and Tan collected the props. The invented slips went in the trial folder, clearly marked. The public map returned to its normal support. The scattered labels were counted back into their box. Luo said the next dragon heading should include a warning about rulers, and Dai told him to write his own fable.

archive_16_054.speaker: narrator
archive_16_054.text: The signed home letter left on the next checked foot-post relay with its actual receipt. Yue kept a copy of her decision, not a copy of her mother's hoped-for answer. She had made the term definite enough that home could now plan around it. Whether the reply would approve was another matter. Tan asked whether she wanted to celebrate signing by improving the lesson immediately. Yue said she wanted to celebrate by eating a plum and refusing to design a better dragon. Tan accepted half the plum when offered, and found it sour enough to make a very unprofessional face.

archive_16_055.speaker: narrator
archive_16_055.text: The morning after the rehearsal, the teacher sent Yue a list of the pupils' further questions. The smallest wanted to know whether dragon headings needed larger shelves. Another asked why a date could be true and still insufficient. Yue placed the questions beside her lesson plan and chose the second for the next preparation interval. She kept the first in the margin rather than pretending it was childish noise. Luo offered to find an ordinary dragon drawing for the public display. Dai said its source should be checked before anybody gave it an appetite.

archive_16_056.speaker: narrator
archive_16_056.text: Tan fitted the accepted storage rail while the room was quiet, with the trained workshop worker supporting the heavier frame. The father had made its adjustment within his limited bench work, and his named fitting credit remained on the accepted slip. Yue moved the lighter wrapped components after the rack was secured and checked. Their own fixed roof stayed dry above the work. The rail's plain usefulness gave Tan more pleasure than she admitted. She ran a fingertip along the clean joint, then caught Yue watching and asked whether she intended to review the grain of the wood.

archive_16_057.speaker: lin_yue
archive_16_057.text: I was wondering whether every good repair looks as though it was always supposed to be there. You worked on the joint for days, and now I can hardly see where the trouble was. I like that. I also think the maker's name should stay somewhere a person can find it when the next joint needs attention.

archive_16_058.speaker: narrator
archive_16_058.text: Tan pointed to the acceptance slip and its makers. Yue grinned, caught in a question which the room had already answered. Not every observation needed to become a new rule. They finished the rail and restored the stored pieces under their actual handling terms. The maker's older notebook had now returned by its agreed village courier loop, with the owner signing its condition receipt. Its damaged margin remained described. Tan put the completed return record on the correct shelf and enjoyed the rare sight of an empty task space without adding another object to it immediately.

archive_16_059.speaker: narrator
archive_16_059.text: The carriage-bridge team sent its next assessment on day one hundred and fourteen. Repair to the approach had begun within the district's existing transport programme. The supplier expected the remaining four hundred and eighty-three food shares, forty charcoal sacks and fifty cooking bundles to leave when the loaded-route inspection passed, with an aimed archive arrival on day one hundred and nineteen. The three additional food shares were replacements for the rejected first carrier, with no extra charge. Dai recorded the new target and requested the actual dispatch receipt before allowing the receiving column to change.

archive_16_060.speaker: narrator
archive_16_060.text: Eight resident days since the close had used eighty food shares and eight cooking bundles. With the accepted first delivery, the store now held three hundred and seventy-two and a half food shares and fifty and a half cooking bundles. Eight cold-day heat sacks, three recovered sacks and the eight new sacks left twenty-eight usable charcoal sacks. Three damp sacks remained excluded. There had been no visiting kitchen meals or overnight guests in that interval. Tan closed the quantities while Yue placed the signed extension in her own papers, where a future contract could not be mistaken for present food.

archive_16_061.speaker: narrator
archive_16_061.text: Sun had found a small blank notebook through the shop's existing village stock, without waiting for the carriage order. She showed it to the teacher on her way home. The cover was brown and imperfectly squared, which she considered suitable for an umbrella with poor manners. Her first page contained only a title and a sentence crossed out so firmly that it could never be reconstructed as a more elegant draft. She told the teacher she was making current work, not leaving a relic. The teacher wished her a troublesome umbrella and a quiet evening.

archive_16_062.speaker: narrator
archive_16_062.text: He Xi returned from the workshop at dusk carrying a paid small parcel for the archive's next local receiver. His father had stayed for the owner's evening bench inventory, checking pieces he could handle safely. His mother was at their village room preparing their own meal after her paid shift. He Xi planned to deliver the parcel, collect its receipt and go straight home. He had drawn Nettle beside the mule route on his school sheet. The drawing looked like an insulted cupboard, and he asked Yue not to show it to the handler.

archive_16_063.speaker: narrator
archive_16_063.text: Luo said the cupboard had excellent load limits. Tan said its legs needed the workshop's attention. He Xi defended the ears and then folded the drawing before further experts arrived. The cook rang the archive's ordinary resident meal bell. He left for his own household while the workers sat down, carrying the returned receipt inside his coat. Snow had stopped, and the yard path looked almost blue beneath the early lamps. Yue ate without waiting for another report, glad that accepting spring had not made every evening an examination of her reasons.

archive_16_064.speaker: narrator
archive_16_064.text: A different bell sounded from the village before they cleared the pot. Its urgent repeated strokes were not an archive signal, and the watcher went to the gate for the actual message. A runner reached the checked path breathless: a fire in the workshop's packing room, the village response crew already there, extra clean blankets and the archive's trained help requested at the safe meeting point. Dai set down her bowl. Tan rose with the rostered emergency kit. Yue heard the word workshop again and thought of He Xi's father checking the small pieces his hand could still hold.
